notes_for_patcher: Three works named in the VERDICTS.md Challenge resolutions have no vault note: 2604.26671 (Zabolotnii, Holinko, and Antonenko), TRIAGE 2605.13414, and 2609.00854. Their evidence is in research/positioning/w4/parts/critic-A/CHALLENGES.md (F Q1 section, lines 213-219; L3 Q1 section, line 116; L4 Q2 section, line 192). 2604.26671 is also mentioned inside [[trace-a-metrologically-grounded-engineering-frameworkfor-trustworthy-agentic-ai]]. Cite these three by arXiv ID with the Critic A attribution rather than inventing note IDs. Keep American spelling, no em-dashes, serial comma, and numbers only from sources.

findings.location: Section 6 (paragraph beginning 'The vocabulary is in use too' and closing paragraph); Section 8 verdict table row 'F | Q1 vocabulary'; Section 10 table row G-FT ('F Q1 (metrology-proper terms)')
findings.issue: The report disagrees with the authoritative VERDICTS.md Challenge resolutions on F Q1. It states that 'Only metrology-proper terms (measurand, GUM uncertainty budget, traceability) are unused for LLM confidence,' grades F Q1 as 'OCCUPIED (validity, psychometric); Prov. (metrology-proper terms),' and lists F Q1 among the cells weakened by G-FT. VERDICTS.md accepts Critic A's challenge: F Q1 is OCCUPIED, including metrology-proper terms, via 2604.26671 (full text) and TRACE 2605.03838. The vault holds the TRACE note, which the report never cites.
findings.evidence: VERDICTS.md F table Q1: 'Metrology-proper terms, at conceptual depth: Zabolotnii, Holinko, and Antonenko 2604.26671 (preprint, April 2026; full text, Sec 1 applies VIM and GUM terms such as measurand and traceability to clinical AI; Sec 10 treats stated-confidence calibration error as an instrument's systematic error) ... TRACE 2605.03838 uses GUM, VIM, and ISO 17025 vocabulary.' Challenge resolutions: 'Accepted. CLEAN (provisional) to OCCUPIED.' Critic A CHALLENGES.md lines 213-219. Vault note trace-a-metrologically-grounded-engineering-frameworkfor-trustworthy-agentic-ai (tagged f-measurement-framing) summary: 'metrologically grounded trust-metric suite mapped to GUM/VIM/ISO 17025; Calibration Error is one listed metric.'
findings.recommendation: In Section 6, replace the 'Only metrology-proper terms ... are unused' sentence with one or two sentences saying that metrology-proper vocabulary is also in use. 2604.26671 (Sec 1 and Sec 10, full text, a conceptual paper with no experiments) applies VIM and GUM terms to clinical AI and calls stated-confidence calibration error 'a direct analog of the systematic error of a measuring instrument.' TRACE [[trace-a-metrologically-grounded-engineering-frameworkfor-trustworthy-agentic-ai]] maps agentic-AI trust metrics to GUM, VIM, and ISO 17025. Add that any exposition using 'measurand' must cite both. In Section 8, change the F Q1 cell to OCCUPIED, with 2604.26671 Sec 1 and 10 and TRACE as load-bearing locations. In Section 10, remove F Q1 from the G-FT row. The Section 6 verdict ('F is OCCUPIED ... used') can stay as written and should add 'including metrology proper.'

findings.location: Section 5 (paragraph 'Three residuals survive', Q2 sentence); Section 8 row 'L4 | Q2'; Section 1.1 sentence 'ABSTRACT-ONLY marks the one load-bearing record'
findings.issue: The L4 Q2 residual is stated without the two matched-budget placebo studies in the corpus and challenge record. 2609.00854 (VERDICTS: 'residual shrinks') shows spectrum-based localization plus infilling losing to blind resampling at matched attempts, with a random-span placebo. 'Try Again, Don't Look Back' (2607.26117, full text in vault, uncited) finds blind resampling beats or ties execution-feedback repair on MBPP+. The report cites only Olausson, Siddiq, and Iscan. Section 1.1 also says NeuroSym-Cal is the one load-bearing ABSTRACT-ONLY record, which stops being true once 2609.00854 bears on L4 Q2.
findings.evidence: VERDICTS.md L4 Q2: 'NARROW (residual shrinks) ... 2609.00854 (concurrent, ABSTRACT-ONLY; found by Critic A): spectrum-based localization plus infilling loses to blind resampling at matched attempts with a random-span placebo. Residual: only that localization comes from the model's own per-requirement confidence, and the prior that it wins is now lower.' CHALLENGES.md line 192: '3:40, p = 3.0 x 10^-9 across three 26-32B models and three benchmarks.' Vault note try-again-dont-look-backblind-resampling-outperforms-self-repair-in-small-code-m: 'MBPP+ at 1.5B/3B/7B; blind resampling beats or ties execution-feedback repair with 2.5-5.5x fewer tokens; conditioning on the failed attempt costs 6.1 points at 1.5B.'
findings.recommendation: In Section 5, extend the Q2 sentence. Matched-budget, placebo-controlled comparisons now exist for test-guided localization (2609.00854, ABSTRACT-ONLY, concurrent) and for execution-feedback repair in small code models [[try-again-dont-look-backblind-resampling-outperforms-self-repair-in-small-code-m]]. Both favor blind resampling, so the residual is only that localization comes from the model's own per-requirement confidence, and the prior that it wins is lower. This also strengthens the 'wrong bet' conclusion. In Section 8, mark the L4 Q2 cell 'NARROW (residual shrinks)' and add 2609.00854 (ABSTRACT-ONLY). In Section 1.1, change 'the one load-bearing record' so that 2609.00854 is also listed as ABSTRACT-ONLY.

findings.location: Section 4.3 (nearest-works paragraph and closing paragraph); Section 2.2 'Contamination (Q3, Q13)' paragraph; Section 10 G-FCS row
findings.issue: The CLEAN (provisional) cells do not list the near neighbors that VERDICTS.md says must be read before any novelty sentence. For L3 Q2/Q7, these are LADDER 2610.34737 (vault note, full text per the L3 interim report), Agentic Self-Awareness 2610.19226 (abstract only), and Not-One-Belief 2610.35694 (vault note, full text). Not-One-Belief is VERDICTS' named nearest non-code work and compares verbal confidence, likelihood, a frozen probe, and P(True) under feedback. For L1 Q13, it is Crossref record 10.1109/tse.2026.3713834 (title only). None of them appears in the report, so the claim that 'no fetched record' measures post-failure updating carries no record of its closest misses.
findings.evidence: VERDICTS.md Challenge resolutions: 'Leads to read before any novelty sentence: LADDER 2610.34737 and 2610.19226 (L3 Q2/Q7, abstract only), and Crossref record 10.1109/tse.2026.3713834 (L1 Q13, title only).' VERDICTS L3 Q2/Q7 nearest list includes 'Not-One-Belief 2610.35694.' Vault note not-one-belief-answer-payloads-persistence-and-dissociated-confidence-signals-in: 'compares verbalized confidence, length-normalized likelihood, a frozen first-turn hidden-state linear probe, and P(True)... the four signals disagree; on Qwen2.5-7B the frozen probe tracks answer persistence rather than truth.' interim-report-l3 line 35 on LADDER: 'Domain-level self-assessment from noisy feedback across 18 models; code not a domain ... the valid-versus-noisy-feedback contrast is being built as a design, at domain not program level.'
findings.recommendation: In Section 4.3, add two sentences to the nearest-works paragraph. Not-One-Belief [[not-one-belief-answer-payloads-persistence-and-dissociated-confidence-signals-in]] compares four confidence signals under conversational feedback outside code and finds that they dissociate. LADDER [[ladder-diagnosing-domain-level-self-assessment-under-noisy-feedback]] builds a valid-versus-noisy feedback contrast at domain level, not on programs, and 2610.19226 probes stated feasibility after a single challenge on Terminal-Bench (abstract only). In the closing paragraph or Section 10, say these must be read in full before the novelty sentence. In Section 2.2, add a clause that one title-only Crossref record (10.1109/tse.2026.3713834) is an unread lead for Q13.

findings.issue: Decomposition sub-question 5 asks whether 'selective prediction, reranking, verifier, cascade, or agent-abstention works subsume' confidence-routed budgets. The draft covers selective prediction, verifiers, and agents, but not execution-based reranking (CodeT, LEVER, MBR-exec), LLM cascades, or agreement- and confidence-driven adaptive sampling. All of these have full-text vault notes, and some are on code. Adaptive-Consistency is the earliest code-inclusive precedent for agreement-driven budget allocation, and Self-Calibration uses trained confidence for early-stopping Best-of-N. A reviewer will name these as prior routing or stopping work.
findings.evidence: lets-sample-step-by-stepadaptive-consistency-for-efficient-reasoning-and-coding: 'stop sampling by agreement; up to 7.9x fewer samples, <0.1% accuracy drop over 17 reasoning/code datasets ... 3.4x on code-davinci-002 ... no calibrated confidence routing vs oracle/random.' efficient-test-time-scaling-via-self-calibration: 'confidence-driven early-stopping Best-of-N ... math/QA; no code.' a-unified-approach-to-routing-and-cascading-for-llms-full-text: 'gains 8% on RouterBench and 14% on SWE-Bench; quality estimates simulated with Gaussian noise.' codet-code-generation-with-generated-tests: 'Dual execution agreement between model-generated tests and code samples selects solutions.' Also cost-saving-llm-cascades-with-early-abstention, zero-overhead-introspectionfor-adaptive-test-time-compute, natural-language-to-code-translation-with-execution, lever-learning-to-verify-language-to-code-generation-with-execution. None is cited.
findings.recommendation: Add two or three sentences to the end of Section 4.2's adjacent-works paragraph or to Section 4.1. Execution-agreement reranking (CodeT, MBR-exec, LEVER) uses confidence to select among candidates, not to allocate an execution budget. Agreement-based adaptive stopping (Adaptive-Consistency, including code-davinci-002 at up to 3.4x fewer samples) and trained-confidence early stopping (Self-Calibration, ZIP-RC; math only) allocate samples but report no random or oracle routing arms. Cascade routing (Dekoninck et al., +14% on SWE-Bench) simulates quality estimates with Gaussian noise rather than real model confidence. Conclude that none subsumes the residual and that they belong in related work. Cite the vault notes.

findings.location: Section 3.4 (trained stated confidence) and Section 7.3 occupant table; Section 9.1 'Main risks'
findings.issue: The report presents CREDO as the only code work training a correctness readout on execution labels. ExecuCritic (2609.16604, full-text vault note, uncited) trains a critic jointly with the coder on the same execution rollouts. It reports a calibrated pass/fail score on HumanEval+, LiveCodeBench, APPS, and SWE-bench Lite, against a frozen prompted critic. This partly occupies the 'trained pass/fail estimator on execution labels with calibration and AUC reported' side of the supervision-matched arm. It is a second code instance of the threat in pivot A14 and should shape the Rank 1 design.
findings.evidence: Vault note execucritic-calibrated-critic-shaping-forcode-generation-with-verifiable-rewards: 'Table 5 reports critic reliability on validation rollouts (HumanEval+, LiveCodeBench, APPS, SWE-bench Lite): ExecuCritic ECE 0.061, Brier 0.137, AUC 72.8 vs frozen prompt critic ECE 0.213, AUC 60.4. Backbones Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct. A separate trained pass/fail predictor, not the coder's own stated confidence; no probe, no verbal-versus-probe comparison. ... NARROWS trained pass/fail estimator on execution labels with calibration and AUC reported; does not trigger pivot 3.'
findings.recommendation: In Section 3.4, after the EpiCaR sentence, add one sentence. ExecuCritic [[execucritic-calibrated-critic-shaping-forcode-generation-with-verifiable-rewards]] trains a separate critic on the coder's execution rollouts and reports ECE 0.061 and AUC 72.8 against 0.213 and 60.4 for a frozen prompted critic (Table 5), again with no probe arm and no own-readout comparison. Add a row to the Section 7.3 table, noting that its status (2609.16604, concurrent) should be confirmed against the A23 window. Optionally note in the Section 9.1 design that a trained critic is a third supervised readout class the paper should distinguish from a trained own readout.

findings.location: Section 5, paragraph 'Three residuals survive' (Q3 sentence); Section 8 row 'L4 | Q3'
findings.issue: L4 Q3 (self-written test adequacy against own confidence) is declared CLEAN (provisional), with nearest works that 'measure adequacy without confidence.' But the corpus holds ValTest, which uses semantic entropy, a model-uncertainty readout, to classify LLM-generated tests as valid or invalid. That pairs a confidence signal with self-written test quality and is closer than either cited neighbor. CodeT (self-written tests used as an agreement signal) and Rethinking Verification (suite thoroughness) are also uncited. The draft's 'nearest' list understates how close the corpus gets to this cell.
findings.evidence: 241108254-valtest-semantic-entropy-test-case-validation-full-text: 'semantic-entropy features classify LLM-generated tests valid/invalid, validity up to +29% and higher pass@1 on HumanEval, MBPP, LeetCode, BigCodeBench; related to L4 self-written test adequacy.' codet-code-generation-with-generated-tests: 'tests written by the same model (label independence caveat; L4 self-written test adequacy).' rethinking-verification-for-llm-code-generation-from-generation-to-testing: 'HumanEval 7.7 tests/problem, MBPP 3 ... Relevant to ... L4 (self-written test adequacy at whole-suite level).'
findings.recommendation: In Section 5's Q3 sentence, add ValTest [[241108254-valtest-semantic-entropy-test-case-validation-full-text]] as the nearest work. It scores the validity of model-written tests from semantic-entropy uncertainty but does not relate the generator's confidence in its own program to the adequacy of its own tests. Mention CodeT [[codet-code-generation-with-generated-tests]] as the self-written-test agreement signal. Keep the verdict CLEAN (provisional) unless the patcher judges that ValTest narrows it; if so, state the residual as 'own-program confidence versus own-test adequacy.' Add ValTest to the Section 8 L4 Q3 'Nearest' column.

findings.location: Section 2.2 'Estimator (Q5)' paragraph; Section 9.1 item 3 and Section 9.2
findings.issue: Q5's estimator-variant sub-part and the Rank 2 contribution both rest on 'ranking changes with estimator.' The draft cites none of the estimator literature in the corpus: smooth ECE, TCE, consistent and unbiased proper calibration-error estimators, statistical inference for score decompositions, and ACE. ACE shows outside code that raw calibration rankings reverse once accuracy is controlled. It is the closest general-NLP analogue of the Rank 2 claim and an extra control (an accuracy confound in cross-model ECE) that the L1 interim report cited and the draft dropped.
findings.evidence: when-calibration-rankings-reverse-accuracy-controlled-evaluation-for-fair-compar: 'ACE accuracy-controlled calibration comparison; raw ECE gaps correlate with accuracy gaps (rho -0.670, n 40); 265 ranking reversals for small-vs-large and thinking-vs-non-thinking. Non-code QA benchmarks.' Listed as source 11 in interim-report-l1-estimator-and-label-oracle-sensitivity-with-contamination-cont. Uncited vault notes: smooth-ece-principled-reliability-diagramsvia-kernel-smoothing, tce-a-test-based-approach-to-measuring-calibration-error, consistent-and-asymptotically-unbiased-estimation-of-proper-calibration-errors-f, statistical-inference-for-score-decompositions.
findings.recommendation: In Section 2.2 Q5, add one sentence. Outside code, ACE [[when-calibration-rankings-reverse-accuracy-controlled-evaluation-for-fair-compar]] finds that raw ECE gaps track accuracy gaps (rho -0.670) and reports 265 ranking reversals under accuracy control, so the protocol needs an accuracy-matched comparison beside the estimator swap. In Section 9.1 item 3, name the estimator foundations once, with smooth ECE, TCE, and consistent estimators as cited foundations (not occupants), so the estimator set is concrete.

findings.location: Section 3.7 'Base versus instruct (Q2a)' and 'Reasoning (Q2b, Q9, Q10)' paragraphs
findings.issue: The general-NLP comparison side of two L2 residuals leaves out corpus evidence that cuts against the stated direction. For Q2a, Tian et al. (Just Ask for Calibration) find verbalized confidence better calibrated than token probabilities in RLHF models, which reverses the sign the GPT-4 report suggests; the L2 interim report relied on this point. For Q9 and Q10, the trace-signal sub-part is CLEAN (provisional) on code, but the draft cites no non-code trace or reasoning-probe evidence: hidden-state probes on R1-distilled models (2504.05419), trace length as an uncertainty signal (2510.10409), and SelfDoubt.
findings.evidence: interim-report-l2-residual-post-training-reasoning-format-on-code line 51: Tian et al. 2305.14975, 'verbalized confidences emitted as output tokens are typically better-calibrated than the model's conditional probabilities ... often reducing the expected calibration error by a relative 50%. This reverses the sign the GPT-4 report implies.' reasoning-models-know-when-theyre-right-probing-hidden-states-for-self-verificat: 'Probes on distilled R1 models verify intermediate answers (Table 1 ECE 0.02-0.10 math) ... no code, no verbal baseline.' trace-length-is-a-simple-uncertainty-signal-in-reasoning-models (arXiv 2510.10409, full text); VERDICTS Q9 cites 2510.10409 as the outside-code side.
findings.recommendation: In the Q2a paragraph, add a clause noting that Tian et al. [[230514975-just-ask-for-calibration-strategies-for-eliciting-calibrated-confidenc-3]] find that post-RLHF verbal confidence beats token probability. The general-NLP direction is therefore readout-dependent, which strengthens the 'by readout' residual. In the Q9 sentence, cite [[reasoning-models-know-when-theyre-right-probing-hidden-states-for-self-verificat]] and [[trace-length-is-a-simple-uncertainty-signal-in-reasoning-models]] as the non-code side of the trace-signal sub-part, matching VERDICTS' citation of 2510.10409.
